selected_frontier.question: Does an exact caller-bound V15/V16 effect capability remain exclusive to one admitted execution context across Linux fork(), or can inherited process memory plus an inherited flock open-file-description preserve/reanimate effect authority in a child?
selected_frontier.why_selected: Current F-V01-09 fresh-main negative evidence already proves stale/unbound V14 attempt admission. The current candidate adds exact V16 identity and a process-local secret, while a parallel stack adds exact-object Gate issuance. Fork inheritance is a cheap discriminator against the assumption that process-local object/secret identity is equivalent to process-incarnation identity.

source_observation: At PR204 head 0e5e227, runtime/state/frank_execution_gate.py returns a plain FrankExecutionLease after flock+V15 acquire and uses a threading.RLock for effect_commit_window; it contains no process-incarnation or Gate-issued exact-object registry.

fork_discriminator_pr233.note: Its OOB accounting is lineage-dependent and should not be assumed globally unique without an explicit macro_cycle_id.

external_primary_evidence.finding: Linux fork children inherit flock locks and inherited descriptors refer to the same open file description.
flock locks are attached to the open file description; duplicated descriptors via fork/dup refer to the same lock and any duplicate can modify/release it.
Python exposes before/parent/child fork hooks for process-local state repair; applicability depends on the fork path returning to the interpreter.
Lease/lock possession alone is not sufficient for external-resource exclusion; the protected boundary must validate a version/sequencer/fencing token.
Snapshot restore can require an explicit revision bump/compaction marker so old generations do not become plausible again.
Side-effect retries need stable request identity and explicit semantics for late/indeterminate outcomes; retry safety is distinct from authority ownership.

out_of_box_experiment.scope: isolated local Linux/Python mechanism replica; not exact Frank runtime
out_of_box_experiment.intervention: Acquire flock on one open file description, register an object in WeakSet, fork once, then inspect inherited registry/lock behavior in child and contender behavior from a fresh open file description.
out_of_box_experiment.interpretation: SUPPORTED_MECHANISM_COUNTEREVIDENCE: fork copies process-local registry state and inherits the same flock-backed open file description. Exact-object/process-local-secret identity therefore cannot by itself be promoted to process-incarnation exclusivity.
limits: Not executed against exact Frank B1/B2/B3 runtime.
Does not prove a reachable production fork path exists.
Does not prove an unauthenticated or external caller can acquire effect authority.
No CPU/RSS/wall benchmark was captured for this microreplica; resource fields remain UNKNOWN.

leading_hypothesis.claim: If Frank permits fork/clone while an execution capability is live, transient effect authority must be bound to an explicit process incarnation (or equivalent non-inheritable capability) and child state must default fail-closed until explicit re-admission/delegation. A Python object identity, copied secret, or flock open-file-description alone is insufficient.

strongest_counterhypothesis.claim: Production Frank can prohibit and measurably enforce all fork/clone paths while any FrankExecutionLease/effect capability is live; therefore no process-incarnation mechanism is needed and a simpler deployment/runtime invariant dominates.
strongest_counterhypothesis.discriminator: Search actual process-spawn/fork surfaces, instrument target runtime, and run exact PR233-style child test. If no fork path is permitted and attempts fail closed before child Python/effect execution, retain the simpler no-fork architecture.

architecture_delta_candidate.name: FORK_SAFE_EXECUTION_CAPABILITY_BOUNDARY
rules: Fork/process cloning is an explicit execution-capability boundary, never an implicit authority delegation.
If child execution is not an admitted feature, inherited Frank execution/effect capabilities become invalid in the child before any Frank semantic/effect path runs.

A child invalidation path must not call LOCK_UN on an inherited flock open-file-description shared with the parent; child cleanup should close/drop inherited physical handles without semantically releasing the parent's V15/V16 execution.

If child delegation is an admitted feature, it requires an explicit new process-incarnation/delegation receipt and an inter-process commit/release protocol; threading.RLock is not a process-shared serialization primitive.
Outcome observation/reconciliation remains admissible after capability turnover because evidence is not effect authority.
At-fork hooks are a candidate mechanism, not sufficient proof; third-party/native fork paths and exec/spawn behavior must be measured.
Do not promote a process-incarnation mechanism if a simpler measured no-fork invariant dominates.
architecture_delta_candidate.rollback: Keep current candidate draft-only; do not merge process/fork hardening until exact target discriminator and normal baselines pass.
